Resolution: total 124…180 step 1, inner 10…100 step 1. Both axes step by one column because the flips the triage found are one column wide, and every cell of every row is asked because the boundary is not monotone in either axis, so a bisection would find one flip and miss the rest.
Legend: .  not generated — the total cannot hold this inner width beside a filler
O  the oracle took the outer break
I  the oracle broke the inner construct instead
T  the oracle took the construct's third break and declined both of the two
?  the oracle broke somewhere this probe does not name

Constructs.Template: public abstract void <name><T…>(int a, int b);
Constructs.InnerConstruct: the type parameter list, against the parameter list
Constructs.ThirdBreak: the gap after the return type, before the method name

Fillers.Description: Every identifier five characters — the control. This is the shape that made a wrap budget of 113 indistinguishable from 118 in a refuted finding, so it is swept deliberately: a threshold that appears only here is a fact about the probe.
Identifier lengths cycling 3…11, so the comma positions land differently at every width.
A wider spread with two long identifiers per cycle, so a given width holds noticeably fewer arguments than under varied-short.

One string literal argument, filling the list on its own — the shape of SK-DIV-0005's named counter-example, `Convert.FromBase64String("…")`, where the inner construct has no comma to break at. Not applicable to a type parameter list.
